tasks.title: CFTR G551D MVP scientifically approved and ready for demonstration
tasks.description:
Milestone definition. Complete only when the CFTR G551D flagship case has passed full scientific review and is ready to demonstrate as a research-use-only mechanism investigation. Scientific sign-off gate — owner Zuhra. Nothing reaches "approved" without her review, per the VMIS provenance rules.

Before this is marked complete:
1. Mechanism correct and sourced — primary = reduced-function gating defect (Class III); defective trafficking explicitly rejected; reduced stability noted as secondary hypothesis. Every factual claim carries a PMID/DOI; facts/inferences/hypotheses separated and labeled; confidence justified by evidence.
2. Variant identifiers pinned/verified — CFTR (HGNC:1884); NM_000492.4 (MANE Select), NP_000483.3; c.1652G>A / p.(Gly551Asp) / G551D; ClinVar VCV000007120 Pathogenic 4-star (NOT VCV000007105); canonical graph ID clinvar:VCV000007120.
3. Known conflicts resolved/disclosed — ClinVar API misparse ("Uncertain" for known-Pathogenic) must not propagate; source from NCBI esummary or local VCF; downstream ACMG "VUS" corrected to Pathogenic or disclosed as a known artifact; VEP Ensembl-vs-pinned-RefSeq transcript difference documented.
4. Safety/scope hold — RUO banner; no diagnosis/prescribing/dosing/"will work" language; therapeutic mentions framed as research hypotheses; contradictions preserved as explicit objects.
5. Demonstrable — cited mechanism note populates the shared VMIS JSON, mechanism graph, phenotype explanation, exportable RUO report; reviewer selects a final outcome via the VMIS scientific review checklist.

Dependency chain: Sakshi's cited mechanism note -> mechanism+phenotype JSON fields -> Zuhra's scientific review -> this milestone.
Reference: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQPHVYBdoW1fQFRlWhUZNJv_gVLoo1ouG1ujxNsGkfQ/edit

tasks.title: Create the VMIS scientific review checklist
tasks.description:
Create the scientific review checklist that must be completed before any VMIS case is approved for demonstration or reporting.
The checklist verifies: correct gene/variant; genome assembly; transcript + version; HGVS genomic/coding/protein; protein ID + AA change; ClinVar + population data accurate; normal gene/protein function correct; mechanism specific to the variant; each variant-to-phenotype step biologically reasonable; major claims have evidence; citations support the exact claims; gene-level evidence not shown as variant-specific proof; facts/inferences/hypotheses separated; weak/missing/contradictory evidence visible; confidence matches evidence; competing mechanisms not hidden; phenotype relationships not overstated; therapeutic statements RUO; no diagnosis/prescribing/dosing; RUO disclaimer present; unresolved issues documented before approval.
Review outcomes: Approved / Approved with revisions / Requires additional evidence / Rejected / Deferred.
Deliverable: a reusable scientific review checklist + sign-off template, applied first to CFTR G551D then other VMIS cases.
Reference: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQPHVYBdoW1fQFRlWhUZNJv_gVLoo1ouG1ujxNsGkfQ/edit

tasks.title: Review the CFTR G551D mechanism note
tasks.description:
Review the completed CFTR G551D mechanism note; confirm the science is accurate, appropriately sourced, and not overstated.
Review: normal CFTR gene/protein function; selected transcript + protein IDs; G551D substitution; gating-defect classification; protein-level consequence; reduced chloride transport; cell/tissue effects; connection to the CF phenotype; competing/secondary mechanisms; confidence per step; supporting citations + evidence quality; separation of facts/inferences/hypotheses; therapeutic/mechanism research language.
Requirements: claims specific to G551D where required; citations support the exact claims; flag gene-level evidence used as variant-specific proof; identify weak/incomplete/contradictory evidence; no diagnosis/prescribing/dosing; therapeutic statements RUO; add review comments; select an outcome via the checklist.
Deliverable: a reviewed note with corrections, unresolved issues, and one final status (Approved / Approved with revisions / Requires additional evidence / Rejected / Deferred).
Reference: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQPHVYBdoW1fQFRlWhUZNJv_gVLoo1ouG1ujxNsGkfQ/edit

tasks.title: Final scientific sign-off for CFTR G551D MVP
tasks.description:
Complete the final scientific review of the assembled CFTR G551D VMIS case before the MVP demonstration.
Review the complete output: variant identifiers + transcript selection; normal CFTR function; variant-specific molecular change; mechanism chain; cell/tissue/phenotype effects; claim-to-source mappings; confidence/uncertainty labels; competing hypotheses; contradictory/missing evidence; mechanism-based research hypotheses; frontend wording + visual presentation; human-review status; RUO disclaimer.
Final approval requirements: every major claim sourced; citations support exactly what's displayed; facts/inferences/hypotheses separated; weak/contradictory evidence not overstated; no unsupported graph relationship displayed; no diagnosis/prescribing/dosing; therapeutic content limited to research hypotheses; all critical corrections done; any unresolved limitation disclosed.
Deliverable: one final decision (Approved for MVP demonstration / Approved with documented limitations / Not approved pending corrections) + reviewer comments + date of sign-off.
Reference: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQPHVYBdoW1fQFRlWhUZNJv_gVLoo1ouG1ujxNsGkfQ/edit

tasks.title: Define what we file vs what we keep as trade secret
tasks.description:
The science/research team (Zuhra + Amina) already worked through what is safe to publish vs what must stay protected while writing the Genetics in Medicine benchmarking paper. Capture that split as a written file-vs-trade-secret boundary counsel and the team can work against.
TRADE SECRET (per Ramesh's June 26 guidance): the exact conflict-resolution mechanism in the MoE engine, the specific weight constants, the tuning. Rule of thumb: disclose the range (e.g. 'k can be 5-10'), keep the optimal value secret.
CAN BE FILED/PUBLISHED: the high-level architecture, the deterministic-reproducibility claim, the relative prioritization of experts (ordering, not numbers), the existence of the M1-M8 modules and the knowledge graph.
CROSS-REFERENCE: must line up with GeneGenius_Provisional_Disclosure.pdf Section 6.3 (intentionally not recited). Boundary doc must not contradict the disclosure.
DONE WHEN: a written file-vs-trade-secret boundary exists, consistent with the disclosure, that counsel and the team can both work against.

tasks.title: Align the defensive-publication plan (Genetics in Medicine paper) with the filing
tasks.description:
Per the three-layer IP strategy confirmed with Ramesh: patent the architecture, keep the mechanism as trade secret, and use the Genetics in Medicine (GIM) benchmarking paper as DEFENSIVE PUBLICATION (prior art once filed, making it hard for others to patent something similar).
TWO HARD RULES:
1. The GIM paper must NOT reveal anything in the trade-secret boundary (see the 'Define what we file vs what we keep as trade secret' task). Check the draft against that boundary before submission.
2. TIMING: the defensive publication should FOLLOW (not precede) provisional #1. If the paper publishes before we file, it becomes our own blocking prior art and can sink the patent. Sequence: file provisional #1 first, then publish.
CONTEXT: GIM leads — Shrinjay (benchmarking), Amina (corresponding author), target submit Oct 2026. Provisional #1 targets mid-July 2026, so timing should be fine — confirm the sequence holds.
DONE WHEN: GIM paper scope checked against the trade-secret boundary AND its submission timing confirmed to fall after the provisional #1 filing date.
